chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Radi says: Some people say this saying is of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), but what confirms that it is the saying of Amīr al-mu’minīn (peace be upon him), is the statement related by Tha‘lab from Ibn al-A‘rābī namely that (Caliph) al-Ma’mūn said: “If ‘Alī had not said ‘Try a man and you will hate him’, I would have said, ‘Hate a man in order to try him’.”

key_terms.اخبُرْ تَقْلِبْ: Try a man and you will hate him
key_terms.اقْلِبْ تَخْبُرْ: Hate a man in order to try him

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'Try a man and you will hate him' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi includes this anecdote from al-Tabari’s *al-Mu’jam* to authenticate the narration’s attribution to Imam Ali (AS), noting that the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun himself acknowledged the superiority of Ali’s phrasing over his own. This scholarly validation underscores the linguistic precision and depth of Imam Ali’s wisdom, framing the act of testing as a divine mechanism for revealing hidden character traits. The incident highlights the competitive intellectual environment of the Abbasid court, where the Ahl al-Bayt’s eloquence often surpassed that of contemporary rulers.
